actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.description: Seed used by the next reset
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: seed

facts.text: Each task is imported as duobench.tasks.<task_id> and registered as the Gymnasium environment duobench/<task_id>, with a <task_id>EnvConfig
DuoBench registers the ball_maze environment as duobench/ball_maze with the BallMazeEnvConfig entry point
The ball_maze instruction is "pick up the board and tilt it so the ball rolls onto the red square"
BallMazeStage has max_stage 4 and five stage texts, from "make contact with the maze" to "task completed; the ball has reached the goal"
TaskStageWrapper.step returns the normalized stage as the reward and the stage tracker's success as terminated
success is stage == max_stage and normalized_stage is stage / max_stage
The info dictionary exposes success, stage, max_stage, current_subinstruction, stage_to_subinstructions and instruction
BallMazeTask.add_task_env wraps the environment in RandomSquareObjsPos and then in BallMazeTaskWrapper
RandomSquareObjsPos.reset draws the object placement from self.np_random and calls the wrapped reset with the seed only at the end
BallMazeTaskWrapper.reset spawns the ball at the start marker, resets the free-joint velocity, runs ten mj_step calls and adds the stage tracker info to the reset info

The ball_maze stage tracker derives its stages from MuJoCo contacts and body positions: 4 when the ball is at the goal, 3 when it left the start area, 2 when the maze is lifted, 1 on arm contact and 0 otherwise
The example action is a dict with left and right arms, each carrying a seven-number tquat and a one-number gripper
The example moves an arm 1 cm with tquat x 0.01, closes the gripper with 0 and opens it with 1
The default config is optimized for teleoperation; the evaluation example switches to absolute joint control, async 30 Hz control and a binary gripper
The evaluation example sets the async control frequency to 30
The FR3 arm model has seven joints, fr3_joint1 through fr3_joint7
VentionSceneFR3Duo uses the vention world scene and the vention height offset as the root frame transform
The upstream requires Python 3.11 or newer
The upstream depends on rcs-core>=0.7.3, av, einops, scipy and tqdm
TaskStageWrapper.step never lets the stage decrease within an episode: it restores the previous stage if the tracker reports a lower one
The README states that the reward is the normalized task-stage progress and that terminated becomes True once the final stage is reached
DuoBench resolves its asset directory from DUOBENCH_PREFIX and defaults it to ~/.duobench
On import, DuoBench downloads the matching asset archive from GitHub if the asset path does not exist

determinism.notes: reset(seed) seeds gymnasium's np_random and the MuJoCo dynamics are deterministic for a fixed state and action; RandomSquareObjsPos.reset draws the object placement from self.np_random before the wrapped reset applies the seed (helper_wrappers.py:187-204), so a new seed reaches the placement on the next reset. The package fake seeds random.Random directly and is deterministic, but it is not the upstream model.

gaps: the fake backend is kinematic: it models no MuJoCo contacts, rigid-body dynamics, ball, board, cameras or robot state, its arm positions and stage thresholds are placeholders, and it ignores the quaternion part of tquat

the action Box bounds and the 8-element observation are placeholders: the clone shows the action dict shape (left/right, tquat and gripper) but states no bounds, and it does not describe the RCS observation; the real environment's spaces are derived by the sim backend, which was not run
the 33.333 ms timestep is the README's 30 Hz evaluation control period (README.md:112); the default teleoperation rate and the MuJoCo physics substep are set by RCS and are not stated in the clone

RandomSquareObjsPos.reset draws the object placement before the wrapped reset applies the seed (helper_wrappers.py:187-204), so the first reset with a new seed may not repeat; the fake seeds random.Random directly instead
reset options are accepted but not modelled: the fake ignores them
the fake returns truncated=False and models no episode time limit; the clone states none for the task wrapper
no rendering and no recording are offered; the real environment imports RCS and downloads the asset archive on first use (README.md:55), neither of which this package does
no physical device is modelled and the benchmark was never validated against a device

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop the runtime refuses step and reset until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the last world state stays readable; the simulator has no native stop
